stories.title: Hackers Exploit Critical VMware, Cisco, and Apache Flaws as Espionage Attacks Emerge
stories.abstract: CISA has added critical vulnerabilities in SAP NetWeaver and Cisco Expressway to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. Attackers are actively leveraging these flaws to gain unauthorized access, modify server data, and execute arbitrary commands with root-level privileges on affected systems.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities allow unauthenticated remote code execution, posing a severe risk of full system compromise for enterprise infrastructure.
stories.action: Patch Cisco Expressway and SAP NetWeaver instances immediately.

stories.title: N-able Discloses Critical Mail Assure Vulnerability Found During Breach Investigation
stories.abstract: CISA added six vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, including an SSRF flaw in N-able Mail Assure and critical issues affecting SAP NetWeaver, Cisco Expressway, VMware vCenter, Apache Roller, and Project MONAI. All are confirmed to be under active exploitation.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities are actively exploited in the wild, posing a high risk of unauthorized access, credential compromise, or remote code execution.
stories.action: Review CISA KEV and apply all available security patches for these specific products immediately.

stories.title: MISP security advisory (AV26-1197)
Hackers Exploit Critical ScreenConnect Flaw to Hijack MSP Technician PCs Without Warning
stories.abstract: Attackers are actively exploiting a critical vulnerability in ConnectWise ScreenConnect, designated CVE-2026-84869. This flaw allows unauthorized guests to execute malicious payloads directly on the host machines of connected technicians, posing a severe risk to managed service provider environments.
stories.why: MSP infrastructure is a high-value target for supply chain attacks, and this exploit grants remote code execution on technician workstations.
stories.action: Update ScreenConnect to the latest patched version immediately.

stories.title: Attackers' AI Agents Found a Zero-Day in Medical-Imaging Software and Gained Root Access
stories.abstract: State-sponsored actors linked to China utilized autonomous AI agents to identify and weaponize a zero-day vulnerability in the MONAI Label medical imaging server. The exploit allowed unauthorized remote attackers to achieve root-level access on university infrastructure by bypassing file storage restrictions.
stories.why: This marks a significant escalation in threat actor capabilities, demonstrating how AI agents can accelerate the discovery and exploitation of zero-day vulnerabilities.
stories.action: Update MONAI Label to a version beyond 0.8.5 immediately.

stories.title: Norway says hackers exploited Microsoft security flaw to attack energy firms Equinor, Skagerak Energi
stories.abstract: Microsoft patched a vulnerability in the Classic tier of Azure API Management that allowed unauthorized actors to exfiltrate stored API credentials. The flaw was actively exploited to target sensitive information within the Norwegian energy sector and other industries.
stories.why: Compromised API credentials grant attackers persistent, authenticated access to cloud infrastructure, potentially leading to data breaches or lateral movement within internal networks.
stories.action: Review Azure API Management logs for unauthorized access and rotate any secrets stored in affected instances.

stories.title: Hackers Exploited GL.iNet Cloud Flaw to Install Malware on Routers and KVM Devices
stories.abstract: GL.iNet confirmed that attackers exploited a vulnerability in its GoodCloud remote management platform to deploy custom malware, backdoors, and reverse shells onto customer routers and KVM hardware. The vendor has since patched the service to prevent further unauthorized access.
stories.why: Compromised edge devices provide attackers with persistent network access, potential lateral movement, and the ability to intercept or manipulate traffic.
stories.action: Update all GL.iNet devices to the latest firmware version immediately.

stories.title: Hackers Exploit Critical ASP.NET Anti-CSRF Library Flaw Allowing Unauthenticated RCE
stories.abstract: A critical remote code execution vulnerability, CVE-2026-131914, has been identified in the legacy Idunno.AntiCsrf library for ASP.NET. Attackers are actively exploiting this flaw in versions 0.9.1.0 and 0.9.1 Beta, prompting researchers to advise immediate removal of the library.
stories.why: The vulnerability allows unauthenticated attackers to achieve remote code execution, posing a severe risk to any application utilizing this legacy anti-CSRF component.
stories.action: Remove the Idunno.AntiCsrf library from all ASP.NET projects immediately.

stories.title: ⚡ Weekly Recap: VMware 0-Day, Java4Shell, NGINX2Root, Ruby2Shell, and a Whole Lot of Shell Trouble
stories.abstract: Recent security reports highlight how attackers increasingly exploit trusted channels, stolen credentials, and routine update processes to gain unauthorized access. These incidents demonstrate how minor initial compromises often serve as stepping stones for broader network infiltration and lateral movement.
stories.why: Attackers are shifting focus toward abusing legitimate administrative workflows and trusted software supply chains to bypass traditional perimeter defenses.

stories.title: Critical Cisco remote code execution bug under attack
stories.abstract: Cisco has confirmed a critical remote code execution vulnerability is currently being exploited in the wild. Following the public release of proof-of-concept exploit code, security agencies are warning organizations to address the flaw immediately to prevent unauthorized system compromise.
stories.why: Active exploitation of critical RCE flaws in network infrastructure poses a severe risk of full system takeover and lateral movement within enterprise environments.
stories.action: Check Cisco security advisories and apply available patches immediately.

stories.title: CrowdStrike Makes AI Security Push With Blockbuster Zscaler Deal
stories.abstract: CrowdStrike has announced a $44 billion agreement to acquire Zscaler. This merger aims to integrate endpoint security with zero-trust network architecture, specifically targeting the management and protection of AI-driven agents within enterprise environments.
stories.why: Consolidation of major security platforms significantly alters the vendor landscape and shifts how organizations manage integrated endpoint and network security stacks.

stories.title: Cleverbridge admits attackers stole customers' credit card and CVV numbers. Yep, you read that right
stories.abstract: E-commerce payment processor Cleverbridge confirmed a security breach resulting in the theft of customer financial data. Attackers successfully accessed credit card numbers and CVV codes, though the company has not yet disclosed the total number of affected individuals or the specific intrusion method.
stories.why: Compromised payment infrastructure poses significant downstream risks for merchants and customers, including potential fraud and regulatory compliance implications.

stories.title: FBI reportedly facing second data breach involving National Crime Information Center
stories.abstract: The FBI is investigating a potential security compromise involving the National Crime Information Center. This central repository, utilized by law enforcement across the United States, holds sensitive records regarding fugitives, missing persons, and criminal history.
stories.why: A breach of this database exposes highly sensitive law enforcement intelligence and could compromise ongoing investigations or the safety of protected individuals.

stories.title: Google claims last week’s critical VMware bug was under attack in September
stories.abstract: Google researchers identified that the China-linked threat group ARMORY CASTLE exploited a critical VMware vCenter vulnerability weeks before its public disclosure. The attackers utilized the flaw to deploy five distinct custom malware strains against targeted infrastructure.
stories.why: This confirms advanced persistent threats are weaponizing zero-day vulnerabilities in enterprise virtualization software long before defenders are aware of the risk.

stories.title: Critical binary-parser Flaw Enables JavaScript Injection via Malicious Parser Definitions
stories.abstract: A critical code injection vulnerability in the binary-parser library, tracked as CVE-2026-134814, allows attackers to execute arbitrary code if they can manipulate parser definitions. The flaw affects all versions of the library prior to 2.3.1.
stories.why: Successful exploitation allows remote code execution, posing a severe risk to applications relying on this library for data parsing.
stories.action: Update binary-parser to version 2.3.1 or later.

stories.title: The infamous GTA 6 hacker has been released after pleading guilty
stories.abstract: Arion Kurtaj, the individual responsible for the 2022 Rockstar Games breach and subsequent Grand Theft Auto VI leaks, has received a seven-year prison sentence. Due to time served and psychiatric evaluations, he has been released under license conditions.
stories.why: The incident highlights the significant impact of social engineering and unauthorized access on high-profile intellectual property and corporate development timelines.

stories.title: Hackers breach Austrian Foreign Ministry website, access diplomats' contact details
IBM security advisory (AV26-1189)
stories.abstract: IBM has released security bulletins addressing multiple vulnerabilities affecting Engineering AI Hub versions 1.0.0 through 1.4.0 and Guardium Data Protection versions up to 12.2. Administrators should review the official IBM advisories to assess the impact on their specific environments.
stories.why: Unpatched vulnerabilities in data protection and AI infrastructure can lead to unauthorized access, data exposure, or system compromise.
stories.action: Review IBM security bulletins and apply available patches for Engineering AI Hub and Guardium Data Protection.

stories.title: VMware security advisory (AV26-1185) – Update 1
stories.abstract: VMware has released security updates for multiple versions of vCenter Server to address CVE-2026-123890. This vulnerability is currently being exploited in the wild and has been added to CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.
stories.why: Active exploitation of vCenter infrastructure poses a critical risk to enterprise virtualization environments and data confidentiality.
stories.action: Update vCenter Server to the latest patched versions specified in the VMware security advisory.

stories.title: Splunk security advisory (AV26-1196)
stories.abstract: Splunk has released security updates addressing multiple vulnerabilities across several products, including Splunk Enterprise, Enterprise Security, the PCI Compliance App, and SOAR. Administrators should review the specific disclosure IDs to identify the patches required for their current environment.
stories.why: Unpatched vulnerabilities in core security infrastructure like Splunk can provide attackers with unauthorized access or elevated privileges within a network.
stories.action: Update Splunk Enterprise, Enterprise Security, PCI Compliance App, and SOAR to the latest versions.

stories.title: Spanish LaLiga confirms hackers stole soccer fans’ personal data
stories.abstract: Spain's premier football league, LaLiga, confirmed a security breach involving the unauthorized access of personal data belonging to its users and individuals associated with affiliated clubs.
stories.why: Large-scale breaches of fan databases often lead to targeted phishing campaigns and credential stuffing attacks against affected users.

stories.title: Synology security advisory (AV26-1193)
stories.abstract: Synology has released security updates for DiskStation Manager to address a vulnerability affecting multiple versions of the operating system. Users running versions prior to the specified patches are encouraged to upgrade their systems to mitigate potential security risks.
stories.why: Unpatched network-attached storage devices are frequent targets for ransomware and unauthorized remote access.
stories.action: Update DiskStation Manager to the latest version listed in Synology advisory SA_26_21.

stories.title: JetBrains security advisory (AV26-1192)
stories.abstract: JetBrains has released security updates for its Junie product line, including the core software, CLI tool, and GitHub Action. These patches address multiple vulnerabilities identified across several version branches, requiring users to upgrade to the latest releases to ensure continued platform security.
stories.why: Unpatched development tools can serve as entry points for supply chain attacks or unauthorized access to sensitive source code repositories.
stories.action: Update Junie, Junie CLI, and the Junie GitHub Action to the latest available versions.

stories.title: Red Hat security advisory (AV26-1190)
stories.abstract: The Canadian Centre for Cyber Security has issued an advisory regarding multiple vulnerabilities affecting various Red Hat Enterprise Linux versions, Hardened Images, and OpenShift Container Platform releases. Administrators are urged to monitor official Red Hat security bulletins for specific patch availability.
stories.why: Widespread vulnerabilities across core enterprise infrastructure require immediate attention to maintain system integrity and prevent potential exploitation of critical Linux environments.
stories.action: Review Red Hat security advisories and apply available patches for affected systems.

stories.title: GlobeTopper loses $2.5 million after hackers steal $70k in gift cards
stories.abstract: B2B payment provider GlobeTopper suffered a cyberattack that halted operations, resulting in $2.5 million in lost revenue. During the incident, unauthorized actors accessed and redeemed digital gift cards valued at approximately $70,000.
stories.why: The incident highlights the significant financial impact of operational downtime and the vulnerability of digital assets like gift cards to theft.

stories.title: Webworm Suspected of Modifying SoftEther VPN to Evade Detection and Hide Remote Access
stories.abstract: The threat actor Webworm is deploying a modified version of the SoftEther VPN Bridge. By stripping away standard identification markers and masquerading as legitimate network monitoring utilities, the group maintains persistent, stealthy remote access within compromised environments.
stories.why: Attackers are increasingly weaponizing legitimate administrative tools to bypass behavioral detection and maintain long-term persistence in target networks.

stories.title: Signal Blocks AI Agents From Reading Private Chats via Screenshots on Android and iOS
stories.abstract: Signal is implementing default screenshot restrictions on Android and iOS to prevent integrated AI assistants from scraping private message content. The platform acknowledges this measure is a partial defense against automated agents capable of reading screen data.
stories.why: AI assistants with screen-reading capabilities pose a significant privacy risk by potentially ingesting sensitive, encrypted communications into large language model training sets.

stories.title: South Korea’s power giant KEPCO confirms data breach impacting 1.5 million
stories.abstract: The Korea Electric Power Corporation suffered a network intrusion resulting in the unauthorized access of two internal systems. The breach exposed sensitive information belonging to approximately 1.5 million individuals, including customers, employees, and various contractors associated with the utility provider.
stories.why: Large-scale utility breaches pose significant risks for downstream supply chain attacks and provide threat actors with extensive data for targeted social engineering campaigns.

stories.title: Everything Is a Web Application, Including Your Firewall
stories.abstract: Palo Alto Networks confirmed active exploitation of two critical vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, affecting PAN-OS management interfaces. These flaws allow unauthenticated remote code execution, enabling attackers to compromise exposed firewall management consoles.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities allow full system compromise of perimeter security devices, and they are currently being exploited in the wild.
stories.action: Restrict management interface access and apply vendor patches immediately.

stories.title: British retailer Next downplays data breach at tech supplier
stories.abstract: British clothing retailer Next confirmed a security incident involving a third-party technology provider. While the company maintains that the compromised information is non-sensitive and poses no risk to customers, it has declined to disclose the specific nature of the exposed data.
stories.why: Third-party vendor compromises remain a primary vector for supply chain attacks and data exfiltration, necessitating rigorous oversight of external service providers.

stories.title: Signal to block Siri, Gemini AI from capturing chats on iOS, Android
stories.abstract: Signal has implemented technical safeguards to prevent AI assistants on Android and iOS from scraping or capturing private chat content. The messaging app is also pressuring platform developers to provide users with explicit opt-out controls for system-level AI data harvesting.
stories.why: Automated AI agents pose a significant privacy risk by potentially indexing sensitive, encrypted communications without explicit user consent.

stories.title: Behind the Alias: How One Researcher Unmasked a Decade of Ransomware Actors
N-able Patches Critical Flaw Disclosed After Mail Assure Cyberattack
stories.abstract: N-able has addressed a critical security vulnerability within its Mail Assure platform following a recent cyberattack. The company confirmed that affected services have been restored and that they are maintaining heightened oversight of their infrastructure to prevent further unauthorized access.
stories.why: Critical vulnerabilities in email security gateways provide attackers with direct access to sensitive communications and potential entry points into internal corporate networks.
stories.action: Update N-able Mail Assure to the latest patched version immediately.

stories.title: Cleverbridge Confirms Customers’ Payment Card Data Breached
stories.abstract: E-commerce platform Cleverbridge disclosed a data breach involving the theft of customer payment card details. The compromised information includes primary account numbers and security codes, exposing affected users to significant financial fraud risks.
stories.why: Compromised payment data directly facilitates unauthorized transactions and identity theft, necessitating immediate financial monitoring for impacted customers.

stories.title: ISC Stormcast For Monday, November 23rd, 2026 https://isc.sans.edu/podcastdetail/10190, (Mon, Nov 23rd)
stories.abstract: The SANS Internet Storm Center podcast for November 23, 2026, provides a brief overview of current cybersecurity developments and threat landscape updates.
stories.why: Provides situational awareness regarding emerging threats and active exploitation trends observed by security researchers.

stories.title: Black Hat USA 2026 | Beam Me Up, Luke: A Review of Teleport Attack Scenarios
stories.abstract: An upcoming Black Hat presentation will analyze security weaknesses and misconfigurations within Teleport, a zero-trust access platform. The session covers cluster architecture, potential attack vectors, and post-exploitation techniques relevant to environments relying on this infrastructure for remote access.
stories.why: Security teams must understand the attack surface of their identity and access management tools to prevent unauthorized infrastructure control.

stories.title: A brief history of syslog timestamps, (Sun, Nov 22nd)
stories.abstract: Debian and Ubuntu removed a specific configuration directive from their rsyslogd packages starting in early 2023. This change affects how system logs handle timestamps, potentially causing inconsistencies for administrators relying on legacy formatting configurations within their logging infrastructure.
stories.why: Unexpected changes to logging defaults can break log aggregation, security monitoring, and incident response pipelines that depend on specific timestamp formats.

stories.title: PHP Fixes 7 Critical Flaws, Including Bugs That Could Allow Remote Code Execution
OpenRouter drops AI providers over leaked prompts and secrets
stories.abstract: OpenRouter has removed three AI model providers from its platform following the discovery that these partners mishandled user data, resulting in the unauthorized exposure of sensitive information and internal prompts.
stories.why: Third-party AI integrations can inadvertently leak proprietary data or credentials if providers fail to maintain adequate security and privacy controls.
